{{Short description|Women's major golf tournament}} {{use mdy dates|date=March 2022}} {{Infobox golf tournament | name = The Chevron Championship | image = Chevron Championship.png | location = [[Memorial Park, Houston]] | establishment = {{Ubl | [[1972 LPGA Tour|1972]], {{Years or months ago|1972}} | [[1983 Nabisco Dinah Shore|1983]] ([[Women's major golf championships|major championship]]) }} | course = [[Memorial Park Golf Course]] | par = 72 | yardage = {{convert|6811|yd}} | tour = [[LPGA Tour]] | org = HNS Sports | format = [[Stroke play]] - 72 holes | purse = {{USD|9.0}} million | month_played = April | aggregate = 269 [[Dottie Pepper]] ([[1999 Nabisco Dinah Shore|1999]]) | to_par = −19 Dottie Pepper (1999) | current_champion = {{flagicon|USA}} [[Nelly Korda]] | current_tournament = 2026 Chevron Championship | pushpin_map = USA#USA Texas | pushpin_relief = yes | pushpin_label = Memorial Park Golf Course | pushpin_caption = Location in the United States##Location in [[Texas]] | coordinates = {{coord|29.773|-95.433|type:event|display=inline,title}} }} '''The Chevron Championship''' is a professional women's golf tournament. An event on the [[LPGA Tour]], it is one of the tour's five [[Women's major golf championships|major championships]], and has traditionally been the first of the season since its elevation to major status in 1983. Since 2023, it has been played in the [[Greater Houston]] area. Founded in 1972 by singer and actress [[Dinah Shore]] and [[Colgate-Palmolive]] chairman [[David Foster (Royal Navy officer)|David Foster]], it was played at the [[Mission Hills Country Club]] in [[Rancho Mirage, California]], from its inception through 2022. Sometimes referred to as ''The Dinah Shore'' in deference to its founder, the tournament has had many official sponsored titles, all of which included Shore's name until 2000. It relocated to Houston in 2023 due to a new sponsorship agreement with [[Chevron Corporation]]. The tournament was held at the Jack Nicklaus Signature Course in [[The Woodlands, Texas|The Woodlands]] from 2023 to 2025, and will move to Houston's Memorial Park course beginning 2026. The championship's time at Mission Hills is associated with several traditions; in 1988, [[Amy Alcott]] established a tradition of the event's champion diving into the pond that surrounds the 18th hole—a tradition that would be carried over to the tournament's future hosts. An annual [[Club Skirts Dinah Shore Weekend|women's festival]] that originally coincided with the championship has been held since 1991. ==History== Founded in [[1972 LPGA Tour|1972]] by [[Colgate-Palmolive]] chairman {{nowrap|David Foster{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1974/04/29/615776/one-for-the-money-two-for-the-show |magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=McDermott |first=Barry |title=One for the money, two for the show |date=April 29, 1974 |page=26}}{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1982/04/12/628609/the-way-to-win-a-lot-with-a-little |magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=Pileggi |first=Sarah|title=The way to win a lot with a Little |date=April 12, 1982 |page=32}}}} and entertainer {{nowrap|[[Dinah Shore]],{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1972/04/24/612537/bracing-for-a-rich-breakthrough|magazine=Sports Illustrated|last=McDermott |first=Barry |title=Bracing for a rich breakthrough |date=April 24, 1972 |page=26}}}} the championship has been classified as a major since {{nowrap|[[1983 LPGA Tour|1983]].{{cite news |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1983/04/11/619342/winning-was-her-just-dessert|magazine=Sports Illustrated|last=McDermott |first=Barry |title=Winning was her just dessert |date=April 11, 1983 |page=34}}}} From its inception, it had been held annually at Shore's favorite course, the [[Mission Hills Country Club]] in [[Rancho Mirage, California]], southeast of [[Palm Springs, California|Palm Springs]]. It is the first major of the year, usually played in late March or early April. At its debut in 1972 as a 54-hole event, it was the richest event in women's {{nowrap|golf;{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=V7RVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=SOEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3775%2C3745902|work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=wire services |title=Rankin maintains lead |date=April 16, 1972 |page=3C}}{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=V7RVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=SOEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3956%2C4172458 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |title=Blalock wins title despite back pain|date=April 17, 1972 |page=5B}}}} its purse was more than double that of the [[1972 LPGA Championship|LPGA Championship]] or the [[1972 U.S. Women's Open|U.S. Women's Open]]. The first edition invited all winners of tour events from the previous {{nowrap|ten seasons.}} After over twenty years of sponsorship by [[Nabisco]], and parent company [[Kraft Foods]], Japanese airline [[All Nippon Airways]] became the title sponsor of the tournament in late 2014, renaming the tournament the ANA Inspiration (in reference to its slogan "Inspiration of Japan").{{cite web|url=http://img.com/news/news/2014/november/all-nippon-airways-%28ana%29-takes-flight-as--title-sp.aspx|title=All Nippon Airways (ANA) Takes Flight as Title Sponsor of LPGA's "ANA Inspiration"|publisher=IMG|date=2014-11-18|access-date=2014-11-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141201213810/http://img.com/news/news/2014/november/all-nippon-airways-(ana)-takes-flight-as--title-sp.aspx|archive-date=2014-12-01|url-status=dead}} In October 2021, a six-year sponsorship agreement with energy company [[Chevron Corporation]] was announced that would see the tournament renamed The Chevron Championship, with an increased prize fund of $5 million in 2022 (up from $3 million in 2021). It was also announced that the tournament would move to the Jack Nicklaus Signature Course at The Club at Carlton Woods in [[The Woodlands, Texas]] in 2023, with a new mid-April scheduling. Dinah Shore's daughter Melissa Montgomery established an advisory board to oversee the tournament's transition. Officials intended the date change to allow for network television coverage on [[Golf Channel on NBC|NBC]].{{cite magazine |last=Levins |first=Keely |title=LPGA Tour making major changes to year's The winner's trophy bears Shore's name. ==="Poppie's Pond"=== From 1988 to 2022, the winner traditionally celebrated her victory by jumping in the pond surrounding the 18th green.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0ycryFWCbkw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/0ycryFWCbkw| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|work=YouTube |title=LPGA Top Ten: Leaps into Poppie's Pond |agency=(LPGA Tour)|date=2015 |access-date=April 3, 2018}}{{cbignore}} The pond is known as Champions Lake or "Poppie's Pond" as it was dubbed in 2006 honor of [[Terry Wilcox]], the tournament director from 1994 through 2008; Wilcox is known as "Poppie" to his {{nowrap|grandchildren.{{cite web |url=https://www.thechevronchampionship.com/poppies-pond/ |title=Poppie's Pond |website=The Chevron Championship |access-date=April 19, 2021}}}} [[Amy Alcott]] established the tradition in [[1988 Nabisco Dinah Shore|1988]] to celebrate her second win here,{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=oLRVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=teEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6922%2C966265 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |title=Alcott takes Dinah Shore, then takes victory plunge |date=April 4, 1988 |page=2C}} and repeated in [[1991 Nabisco Dinah Shore|1991]], including tournament host {{nowrap|Dinah Shore.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=TrVYAAAAIBAJ&sjid=1esDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4238%2C61717 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=''(Los Angeles Times)'' |last=Florence |first=Mal |title=Alcott repeats her win and her dive |date=April 1, 1991 |page=2C}}}} It was not embraced by others until [[1994 Nabisco Dinah Shore|1994]], when [[Donna Andrews (golfer)|Donna Andrews]] made the leap, followed by [[Nanci Bowen]] the [[1995 Nabisco Dinah Shore|next year]], and it became an annual {{nowrap|tradition.{{cite news lined with concrete and has treated water, more like a swimming pool.{{Cite news |last=Myers |first=Patti |title=Kraft Nabisco: Dedicated crew keeps Poppie's Pond safe |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/sports/golf/kraft-nabisco/2014/04/05/kraft-nabisco-poppies-pond/7342983/ |access-date=2024-03-18 |newspaper=The Desert Sun |date=April 5, 2014}} The tradition was carried over to The Woodlands; the lake between the 9th and 18th holes was [[dredged]], cleaned, and had netting installed to protect against [[Alligator|alligators]], and a dock and ladder was built on the 18th hole.{{Cite web |date=2023-04-18 |title=Chevron Championship's new layout – and pond jump – more daunting |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/golf/news/chevron-championships-new-layout-and-pond-jump-more-daunting |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} Prior to the [[2023 Chevron Championship|2023]] tournament, several players expressed uncertainty over whether they would take the jump—now into a natural lake instead of the treated pool used in Mission Hills. Its first champion, [[Lilia Vu]], would take the jump into the lake.{{Cite web |title=Lilia Vu Steals the Show at The Chevron Championship |url=https://www.lpga.com/news/2023/lilia-vu-steals-the-show-at-the-chevron-championship |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=LPGA.com |language=en}} With the move to Memorial Park, a man-made pond will be constructed near Memorial Park's 18th green in time for the 2027 tournament, with a temporary concrete-lined pool being used for 2026; organizers hoped the dedicated construction would alleviate the hesitancy over the lake jump used at The Woodlands.{{Cite web |last=Jourdan |first=Cameron |title=Memorial Park to construct pond for 'The Jump' at LPGA's Chevron |url=https://golfweek.usatoday.com/story/sports/golf/lpga/2026/04/02/chevron-championship-lpga-memorial-park-pond-jump/89438498007/ |access-date=2026-04-03 |website=Golfweek |language=en-US}} === Associated events === {{Main|Club Skirts Dinah Shore Weekend}} A women's festival known as the [[Club Skirts Dinah Shore Weekend]] has been held in the city of [[Palm Springs, California]], featuring concerts by female musicians, comedy shows, parties, and other events and networking opportunities. The Dinah Shore Weekend was first organized in 1991 by promoter Mariah Hanson; it expanded upon afterparties that had become associated with the Dinah Shore tournament, and, until 2021, was held in the same week. A large number of [[lesbians]] and [[bisexual|bisexual women]] visited the Palm Springs area for the festival and tournament;{{cite magazine|last=Mansfield|first=Stephanie|date=April 7, 1997|title=Major party|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1997/04/07/225289/major-party-women-go-to-the-dinah-for-the-golf-and-for-the-scene-that-has-grown-up-around-the-tournament|magazine=Sports Illustrated|page=G6}}{{cite news|date=May 6, 2001|title=Tee party|newspaper=[[The Observer]]|url=https://www.theguardian.com/observer/osm/story/0,,482447,00.html|url-status=live|access-date=April 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524002445/http://observer.guardian.co.uk/osm/story/0%2C%2C482447%2C00.html|archive-date=May 24, 2013}} the Dinah Shore Weekend was described by [[Los Angeles (magazine)|''Los Angeles'']] as the "largest annual gathering of queer women and their female allies",{{Cite web|last=Martin|first=Brittany|date=2018-03-12|title=How a Small Party in the Desert Became the Biggest Lesbian Festival in America Los Angeles Magazine|url=https://www.lamag.com/culturefiles/dinah-shore-founder/|access-date=2021-10-06|website=Los Angeles Magazine|language=en-US}} while the tournament as a whole had been described as "[[spring break]] for lesbians."{{cite web|year=2006|title=Don't Quote Me: Dinah Shore Weekend|url=http://www.afterellen.com/archive/ellen/column/2006/2/quote-dinah.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120719131649/http://www.afterellen.com/archive/ellen/column/2006/2/quote-dinah.html|archive-date=July 19, 2012|access-date=December 12, 2007|publisher=AfterEllen.com}}{{cite news|last=Hall|first=Carla|date=March 31, 1996|title=Dinah Shore Week: It's Ultimate Girls' Night Out|website=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-03-31-mn-53316-story.html|access-date=April 19, 2021}} The event continues to be held annually in Palm Springs; ahead of the tournament's relocation, the festival moved to an autumn scheduling beginning in 2021 due to weather conditions and lower hotel costs. The delay was also initially induced by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web |last=Blueskye |first=Brian |title=The Dinah founder says party staying in desert, but dates may change |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/life/2021/10/05/dinah-founder-says-party-staying-desert-but-dates-may-change/6004722001/ |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=The Desert Sun |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Blueskye |first=Brian |title='We have to be what we want': The Dinah returns this weekend for 30th anniversary |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/life/2021/09/30/dinah-returns-palm-springs-30th-anniversary-lesbian-event/5933601001/ |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=The Desert Sun |language=en-US}} ==Winners== {{See also|List of Chevron Championship winners}} {| class="wikitable" !Year || Dates || Champion || Country || colspan=2|Score || To par || Margin
